policy: Records exactly source-backed open questions and non-executed future tests. This register grants no runtime permission or owner approval. Updates to original research require matching refreshed register and separate governance review.

questions.question: What canonical reference identifies a worker independent of OS PID, job and node?
Which proof binds a principal to that worker/node on each supported platform?
How is announcement issuer authenticity/replay/revocation verified?
What source and expiry make an observed capability/health descriptor current?
What jointly coherent M09 snapshot+lease evidence can qualify current per-action resource admission?
How is reverse M11 owner liveness bound/authenticated without interpreting `M11:` prefixes as signatures?
How are exact host/OS/accelerator and unsupported-platform capabilities described safely?
Which registry fields, if any, may cross node/project/tenant/public API boundaries?
What exact work/attempt/epoch binds an advertisement to a separately authorized action?
Which observable state distinguishes discoverable, reachable, running and owner-controllable?
How are host clock skew, partitions and local-vs-remote identity handled?
Who verifies installed adapter/provider/task compatibility and qualified versions?
How are composite member grants and mismatched expiry/revocation handled without partial admission?
What worker retirement/draining lifecycle would invalidate stale announcements?

What permission-filtered provenance/telemetry can be retained without leaking tenant/node secrets?

What evidence bounds copy/IPC/PCIe/NVLink/host staging latency and net benefit without guessing throughput?
What authenticated authority permits peer or cross-process memory sharing and revokes it?

What does failure of one member mean for still-running peers and OS cleanup rights?

What checksum, rights and remote artifact/export guarantees are required after cloud interruption?
What evidence simultaneously qualifies a composite multi-device grant and worker controls after one GPU fails?
What default future policy applies when any owner proof is missing, stale, conflicted or unsupported?
